utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. All the accused are present. Prosecution we have Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Vanderpuye, Ms. Soljan. I can't see him -- sorry, Mr. Mitchell. But the column is in the way, so I couldn't see you. Absent amongst the Defence teams I notice Mr. Nikolic and Mr. Bourgon and I think that's it. I think that's it. Okay, the witness is -- yes, Ms. Nikolic you are announcing?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I would just like to present to the Chamber and my colleagues Mr. Dragan Dukic, a new member on our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And you are most welcome, Mr. Dukic. Mr. Vanderpuye, you've finished. Mr. Lazarevic, you are to start today, half an hour maximum so that the gentleman can make it to the airport in time. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Ristivojevic, I will do my best to finalise my direct examination within the time limit allocated to me by the Chamber. In order to avoid any kind of confusion I would kindly ask you to speak slowly. During your yesterday's testimony, on page 92 of the transcript you spoke about the failure to provide assistance as a crime provided by the criminal code. According to your recollection, what was the sentence that this crime carried?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the maximum sentence that this crime carries is one year imprisonment, and there was no specified minimum sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. One more question in this regard, could a perpetrator of this crime be an official or any physical entity?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anyone. The law says whoever, which means that any individual can be the perpetrator of this crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Defence team of Mr. Borovcanin already questioned Mr. Bajagic, an expert in the structure of MUP, the police forces staffs, the PJP units, the special police brigade, and other subject related to police work. Since on a number of occasions you were asked about some of these topics, can you tell me whether these topics were the subject of your report? Did you analyse them in any respect in any detail?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, and that is what I said yesterday. I am not an expert in police work in general, and how it is organised or how it operates. Whenever I was asked a question in this relation, I think I emphasized that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the units mentioned in Order 64/95 dating the 10th of July, which we are already extensively discussed, in your expert report did you at all tackle or address any other unit that you were questioned about during the cross-examination by my learned friend, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you were questioned by my learned friend, Mr. Ostojic, and that's on pages 28007 and 008, it was suggested to you that resubordination ceases once a combat task is accomplished and that on the 12th of July, 1995, as it says in the transcript, there were no enemy offensives in the Srebrenica sector. Do you remember that part of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Since the position of our Defence team is that the enemy offensive was finally finished by the breakthrough and the reaching of the territory under the control of the BH army, and that in that period Mr. Borovcanin mentioned the general area of Bratunac and Zvornik was resubordinated to the VRS, can we just look at a couple of documents relevant to this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the Chamber, since this witness for the most part was involved in analysing rules and regulations rather than the facts, I would just like to highlight a couple of documents, and I will mention others only for record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we first look at document P47, please. That's a report issued by the Main Staff of the VRS addressed to the president of Republika Srpska and dated the 30th July, 1995. Can we look at page 3, item 6 (b) in B/C/S; and in English, it's on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, item 6 (b) states that units of the Drina Corps are at full combat readiness and that the subordinated units of the corps, specifically the 1st Bratunac and the 1st Milic Brigades were involved in scouring the terrain, and so on and so forth, as stated in this report. From this document can one deduce that combat activities are still ongoing on the 13th of July in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Number one, this is leading. The second issue is that this witness has repeatedly testified that he's not a military expert, and he's not able to determine when a combat operations commences and finishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Vanderpuye seems to be right, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly what I intended to say. I said that yesterday, and I told that to Mr. Ostojic as well, and I would repeat the same answer, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. For record, I would just like to mention with regard to this copy -- topic the following documents deal with the events that took place after the 13th, i.e., the combat operations and the involvement of MUP units in these operations after the 11th and the 12th; and these are exhibits P136, P137, P138, P139, P140, P48, P49, P3061, and I'm not going to go on. This is quite a few documents that we are dealing with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you proceed I notice, Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am not sure if it's an argument or a question. If, of course, these documents can be presented to you, but maybe not in front and through the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I most certainly didn't show any of these documents at all to the witness. I just enumerated them for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed, and we'll see where we get.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to resubordination of MUP units, let us look at document 1D1045, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You are going to see it shortly. In e-court, that's a request be the Drina Corps command dated the 15th of July, 1995. It is, of course, addressed to the Zvornik Milic and Bratunac brigades as the units subordinated to the Drina Corps and their request reports to be submitted about the engagement of forces. Paragraph one mentions MUP units as well. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It says: "Report where units -- your units and MUP units in your area of responsibility are asked -- are engaged."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. And so just one question regarding this document. Given the date that this document bears, which is the 15th of July, 1995, does this document tell us anything about resubordination of MUP units and their engagement in the activities on this date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think the witness should maybe read the first paragraph first and then he can maybe answer the questions. I think the way the question was put to him was completely unconnected to the document as presented to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I am not opposed to it. The witness has the document in front of him, and he will be able to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In the meantime I suppose he's had already a chance to look at it, having heard Madam Fauveau. Let's proceed with your question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this is a report about the use of the forces of the Drina Corps, because the situation in the field was quite confused and a report is demanded to be submitted about the location of the Drina Corps units and the MUP units in your area of responsibility. The references is probably to the MUP units that were subordinated to the Drina Corps because they were in its area of responsibility, but that's my assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad the witness qualified his answer. It is a speculative answer because the document itself doesn't refer to the specific units that were resubordinated pursuant to the July 10 document that my colleague referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to record to be clear on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move ahead. Let's move ahead and try to avoid as much objections and comments so that we finish with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The next document I would like us to look at is 5D1346. If we could look at it in e-court. It's an order from the Drina Corps command. Again, the date is the 15th of July, 1995. Let us look at this part where it says item 1. Again, the MUP forces are mentioned as are the attached units, the date is the 15th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 1, please, of this order. So it says here based on the latest developments in the general area of Zvornik, the commander of the Drina Corps decided that elements of the 1st Zvornik Brigade and of the POSSS should return to their area of responsibility, so this is what is of interest to me. We are talking about attached units. So this is an order from General Krstic to the MUP force and the attached units; is that so?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, before answer the question. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe, Your Honour, the witness could tell us who this order was sent to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's combine that together with your answer to Mr. Lazarevic's question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says here, you can see yourself in the upper part --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says ZPPBR, I suppose that this acronym stands for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. And it says here that they should go back to their area of responsibility in order to prevent any consequences of the -- any attack on Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's note, could the speaker please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please slow down. Try to answer the question. I think you are.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are already going beyond the question, so you don't need to go any further. Your next question, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does this order pertain to MUP units too, to cut the long story short?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says here in the order that the Zvornik Infantry Brigade with the MUP forces and detached units would carry out the task that is indicated here, that's what it says in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can we consider this as a new combat tasks for -- task for the MUP units in relation to the task that we had an opportunity to discuss regarding order number 64/95?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, that's leading and it also calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But we have the answer now, let's proceed. You rose too late. The answer was already there. Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to look at P927. It's an order of the commander of the VRS Main Staff, dated the 17th of July, 1995, pertaining to the unification of operations. And I would like us to look at item 1 in this order. Could we please zoom in so that you can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In item 1, three officers from the Main Staff are dispatched to provide assistance to unify the VRS and MUP forces, to plan and coordinate combat operations, to block and route and destroy the remnants of the Muslim forces. Can we see from this document anything about the use of the MUP units in combat operations on the 17th of July?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, I need some time to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: While he reads it, Mr. Lazarevic, yesterday and also last week, you spent I don't know how much time standing and sitting and standing up again complaining that the witness was being asked questions which went outside the area of expertise, and you are doing exactly the same as your colleagues did when you were objecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's true. However, some suggestions have been made to this witness by the Defence of -- by my colleague, Mr. Ostojic, in relation to resubordination and the continuance of combat activities by the units MUP; so I believe I am entitled to try to clarify this with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By now, you should know what our position is in relation to statements made by expert witnesses on matters that fall outside their area of expertise. I think we have made that clear already. Anyway, are you in a position to answer the question, please, Professor? And if questions are put to you that fall outside your area of expertise and you think you should not answer them, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat your question now that I have read the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, can we see anything about the participation of the MUP units in combat operations on the 17th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I read the first item here, I can see that together with the VRS forces, they should continue destroying the remnants of the Muslim forces in the sectors of Kamenica and Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I would like us to look at another document, in fact I only have two questions for you and then we are done with your re-examination. The document is P5D1320. And I would like to ask you a question regarding this document. It's a dispatch from the offices of the Minister of the Interior, the date is the 11th of July 1995 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's correction: June.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it's in fact a forwarding of a dispatch that bears the same date. Could we please look at the bottom of this document, and you can see the president of Republika Srpska has orally ordered the use of all the available forces of the MUP units of Republika Srpska from the municipalities that are listed here: Robatice [phoen], Visegrad, Gorazde, Rudoj [phoen], Cajnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And could you please read the document through and then I will ask you a question?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am reading it. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You were asked some questions about the order 64/95. That's dated the 11th of June, 1995. And if you look at this document, did this indicate the legal procedure that you spoke about in your examination-in-chief, the legal procedure that you spoke about regarding the use of the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? I don't understand what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, in light of this document you can see that there is an oral order issued by the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And then the commander of the Main Staff is now saying, take immediate measures through competent organs of the RS MUP in the above-mentioned municipalities, that the personnel be called up and dispatched to the 14th HL Infantry Brigade who should be used on the demand of the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this the legal procedure that you were talking about when you were speaking about document 64/95, about the use of the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I see this dispatch here and it does describe the legal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely my question.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it describes the legal procedure, but I can't see, so to speak -- well the procedure is described here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. My last question, when you were asked questions by Mr. Ostojic, you were also asked about reporting, quite specifically, whom should the chief of the SJB Zvornik should send his reports to. That's at page 15 of the transcript yesterday. I would now like us to look at the Exhibit 3115 dated the 15th of July. It's a dispatch from the commander of the staff of the security services centre in Zvornik notifying about the situation in the area of the centre. If we could look at the upper part of this document. Could we please look at the addressees. We can see here the Republika Srpska MUP at Pale, then the cabinet of the minister, the VRS Main Staff, the MUP of the Republika Srpska, the minister, the command of the Drina Corps, the forward command post of the Drina Corps, Attention General Krstic, and the command of the 1st Zvornik Brigade and the 1st Bratunac Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What can we conclude on the basis of this document regarding the reporting procedure, reporting on the part of the public security centre? According to this document, who receives reports from it, only the organs within the Ministry of the Interior or other structures or other organs too.

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on this document, some units in the corps, the corps command, the Main Staff, so it's a very broad circle of addressees. And here we can see the president of the republic, the minister, and some commands are mentioned here quite specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ristivojevic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I notice Madam Fauveau. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to put one single question to the witness relating to the previous document, 5D1320, describing the procedure applicable when police units are subordinated to army forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's hear the question and then decide whether to allow it or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a question relating to June 1995, completely unconnected to what happened in Srebrenica, and I wanted to ask the witness whether in any documents that he has consulted himself, he has ever come across a similar document relating to subordination of police units to army units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... document again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Talking about July 1995, of course, and Srebrenica, which is what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are agreed here to allow the question. So you can answer it, Professor. We can finish your testimony here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, could you please repeat your question now? I have read the document once again, so your question is?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Relating to the Kravija operation in Srebrenica in July 1995, did you ever see a document from the police services or the president of the republic outlining the procedure similar to what you saw in 5D1320, i.e., informing the VRS that the police would be subordinated to it?

utterances.speaker: BRANISLAV RISTIVOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, so have I seen any documents that were sent to the military informing the military that the police would come and be resubordinated to the army? No, no I cannot recall any. Not in the documents that I went through, apart from this document. So any other document that -- whereby somebody would inform them about that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, he is being -- now speaking into the microphone but we haven't been receiving interpretation. Let's bring it to an end as quickly as we can, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to know whether the document that the witness is referring to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... see this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... is a document that he can read to us from. He mentioned a document of the 10th of July, 1995, which apparently he has in his brief. Could he maybe tell us who this was destined to, this order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my colleague had the document to ask him in relation to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: She just -- she is not to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we have no finish here because at the end of the day you are only allowed one question, Madam Fauveau. This bring the testimony of the expert witness to an answered. I would like to thank you for having been kind enough to come not once but twice to give evidence, and I also, on behalf of the Trial Chamber, wish you a safe journey back home. I hope you make it on time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, for the record although I don't think I need to repeat it because I said it yesterday, we are still sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis for the same reasons explained yesterday. Documents, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I think our list has already been tendered. We did -- we sent the wrong one, obviously. I am sorry. I will just have to check this. Maybe we can deal with this at a later stage just to make sure that everything is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. On the meantime the Popovic Defence team has one document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We sent the list just for one document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which is 1D1316. Any objections, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not in relation to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any other objections from any of the other Defence teams? None. So your document, Mr. Zivanovic, is admitted. Beara Defence team, you have three documents that you wish to tender, P24, if that is not already tendered. 5D1389 and 2D615. Any objections, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have an objection for these two documents, 5D1389 and 2D615. In respect to this first document, it wasn't commented by witness at all. I mean, the witness, obviously, didn't make any comments in relation to this document and I don't see the basis for admission of this document through this witness. As for 2D615, I don't believe that this document is reliable. The witness was -- this expert was asked questions in this respect, and he gave an explanation; and I believe that in order to -- to tender this document into evidence, there needs to be an additional -- an additional proofing of these of these facts which were stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any further comments from anyone? Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We have no remarks with respect to either of these two documents. No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to document 2D615, I know they claim it's unreliable, but I didn't hear a basis for it. So I would be curious to know why they think it is unreliable. We did a hear from the witness and we heard his prefatory comments. First he didn't know an incident. And then you actually pretty well that the incident involved purportedly another person. I think it is reliable. I think the practice was that we would introduce these types of material when it goes to issues of credibility, which I think it does. With respect to the other document, I still believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I stop you here. Is it your position, therefore, that you don't believe the witness in his statement that that document doesn't refer to him but mistakenly and that the incident occurred that was referred to in that document refers to someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, carefully reviewing the witness's testimony, he first denied anything knowing about an incident. Then he certainly knew about it and then he claimed that it was someone else, not him that was involved in it. It clearly identifies him on the document. We believe that it is what it is, although he testified that it was some other individual, I think the document is reliable on its face. It is an international organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we think that unless they brought in other articles that this witness claims exists as to who -- who was involved in these two incidents, we believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Defence lawyers were called --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's two instances, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in their re-examination, I think they could have as they did with other documents bring it up to the witness to show these articles that the witness claims exists from some newspaper that he didn't identify claiming that he wasn't involved in the incident. But it's not that big of a point for us. I think the Court heard the evidence, have seen the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm very glad to hear you say this. It's certainly not a big point to us. I don't see the point of admitting this document in the first had place unless there is disagreement. If, however you want to pursue the matter further later on and bring evidence in relation to the alleged incident as it may relate to this last witness, then, of course, we will review our position. With regard to 5D1389, what's your position in relation to the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought we covered it with him. Off the top of my head I don't know that. I can take a look at it, if he says we didn't we will bring it in through another witness, certainly. But I think we covered a whole host of documents, this is one of them, and I think this expert -- or this witness actually looked at it, and he gave some comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's admit only P0024, for the time being. The other 615 is not being admitted. 1389, we reserve your rights to have it admitted later on through someone else. Thank you. We do have the lists, now, Mr. Lazarevic. Why is mine thicker? Let's proceed. We have a three-page -- four-page list here. Any objection from the Prosecution to any of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in all honesty I will need a little bit of time to go through these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Other Defence teams? Same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we'll come back to you after the first break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, Mr. McCloskey, and Ms. Fauveau, I suppose you have had a chance to discuss a little bit? I take it that we are first proceeding with Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Madam Usher. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We will be prepared to cross-examine Mr. Mijatovic on any issues of -- involved. However, we also -- if you don't feel it's necessary, it may not be necessary given the issue -- and the limited issue, so we also won't take offence if you don't think it's necessary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same here, Mr. McCloskey, we don't know either if we are going to ask any questions once we have given the -- the opportunity to Mr. Zivanovic to put his questions first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We will be able to go into issues of credibility and such, but given that that's really not the issue at hand, it may not be, but I guess we will cross that bridge when we come to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. I notice that you have already taken the opportunity to salute the accused, but before you proceed, we proceed with your testimony. If you could kindly go through the solemn declaration again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable. Mr. Zivanovic is going to ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Before I start my examination-in-chief, I would like to inform this Trial Chamber that we got two verification of accuracy of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have seen them here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: However, I found so far --found another error in translation. It is related to the page 21946, lines 5 to 15. It is in the first sentence precisely I read it in -- I read it in B/C/S: [Interpretation] "During -- I ascertained that in relation to July 1995, according to statements given by the hotel's employees, someone - and they don't know who this was - had seised the journals and the books from July, precisely." [In English] And in translated part of this document, the word journals, "zurnali," was not translated. Just the books. So two B/C/S words, "zurnali unjga," were translated with just one word, one English word, "books." So it myself arise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The confusion in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you for clarifying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As usual, you are very matriculate in your work. Mr. Zivanovic, I suppose we can now proceed with your questions, and I would suggest you explain to the witness the reason why he is here again; in other words, that it is not something capricious, something that we felt the need for. I also noticed you, Mr. Mitchell, standing up and suddenly sitting down again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, we agree with the change, but the word, "zurnali" has been consistently translated as "logbooks," and we would like to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the correct version of the transcript, the word journals, "zurnali," was not translated at all, just the word, "knije [phoen]," books; it is a point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We agree that was untranslated. I am just saying that the word, "zurnali" has been translated as "logbook." That's the -- that's the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. It is so translated in the last one, that we have received anyway regarding page 21917 lines 5 to 10. All right. Let's proceed, thank you. Both of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I told you already why you must reappear before this Tribunal, but I am about to tell you again. The need has arisen for you to clarify certain elements of your evidence, more specifically in relation to your work in terms of covering documents at Fontana Hotel in Bratunac. That is the only thing that we shall now be focussing on. Thank you. First of all, can you please tell me what assignment you got from me as lead Defence counsel about the activities regarding the Fontana Hotel? Can you tell us that, please?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The task is short and clear. I was told to go to Bratunac to go to Fontana Hotel and to find any evidence on Vujadin Popovic having spent a night there in July 1995. If possible, I was also told to make copies of any documents found and to hand the whole thing over to you. That was the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you dispatched to look for a particular document?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing that was mentioned at the time was for me to try and track down this information in the guest book dated 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me who you were in contact with in order to accomplish this mission of yours?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the verification procedure or right away?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, who did you first get in touch with? Who was the first person?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I spoke on the phone to Brana Ilic who, for a long time, was the only person who was on duty as it were every day at Fontana Hotel. He was the only person who could provide answers to matters such as these.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So what was if feedback you got from him when you finally spoke to him?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I had asked him a question about who owned the hotel and who I should seek out in order to apply for this sort of official procedure. He said they had a manager who was from Bijeljina and then dropped a name on me that I failed to memorize. I asked Brana to get in touch with this person, because they spoke often anyway, in order to inform them that I was there, in order to gain entry to the hotel and accomplish my mission there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you agreed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I had received permission to access the hotel. This is something that Brana eventually conveyed to me. Four days after you gave me the mission, I went there with Brana and we tried to track down the document that you required or, rather, the information that you required.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Once you were there, what happened next at Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: After -- soon after I met up with Brana he took me to the cellar of Fontana Hotel. This is a dark area, no natural light and it's not particularly tidy, either. He took me to an area that appeared to be a closed room, some sort of a room. I don't know what it was used for, or rather it wasn't closed. It was an open-plan room. There was some shelves there and on one of those there was a heap of loose sheet of paper. It was an untidy scene. They had probably had been lying around that place for years and then he started skimming through these loose sheets of paper. Soon after he turned around, looked at me, and told me that whatever it was that we were looking for was certainly not there. Right after this we left the hotel. A hundred metres further down that street, we were off to what he referred to as the directorate or the management. I didn't know that that place was the management of Hutro Podrinje, which is a catering association, a local one from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to interrupt you here. I would like to have a clarification from you on one point. We are going back to the hotel itself?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that much is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This room that you mentioned, where exactly was it? What part of the building? Can you be more specific about that?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: You take the entry and then on the left-hand side is reception. Right next to reception there is a staircase taking you down to the basement of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just another thing, you mentioned shelves where these sheets were stacked. Was it just on these shelves or were they lying elsewhere on that room, too?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, we talked about that room in the hotel. It wasn't like they were proper shelves. This was the a protruding section of the wall. I'm not sure how to put it. It resembled a shelve to some extent, but there was this one bit of wall jetting out and that's where we found this lot of loose sheets, a whole mound.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the only place, this shelf-like place, the section of the wall jetting out, was that the only place with sheets of paper?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I turned around to look around me and that was the only place. Everything else was much the same as elsewhere in the hotel apart from the section that was still being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. My understanding earlier on was a bit different but not you set the record straight. Now, you're off to the management building as you said. Can we pick it up from there?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Brana got the key, and he unlocked the door. The key was in his possession. The archive was, so to speak, under his control but under lock and key; and he had a key. It was a musty room and the roof was leaking. It was the office of his company, and then he went without hesitation straight to a place where he appeared to believe he could track this information down for me. I simply followed him into that room. It was an office, as a matter of fact. I hadn't read the tack on the door, I didn't know what this room was. Nevertheless, Brana started going through the documents there one by one inspecting the documentation that was there. First of all, he was looking for the guest book which I believe was the right thing to do, because that was my reasoning, too. This, I believed, would provide us a shortcut to the information that we were after. Get the guest book for July, that's what we had been told. However, he soon gave up the search because he realised soon enough that there was no way he could possibly it there. He knew some things, he didn't know some others, but if there was something new about this he would have found it immediately. And he realised there was no guest book. The search continues. We were off to another part of the room where he had began rummaging through sheets of paper that were folded three times, as it were; and they were stuck up into what I can only refer to as a complex shape. And then I said, Brana what is this? What do you think these are called, the documents that you are after? And he said, These are journals. I had never heard that one before. I walked up to this heap of papers, and I had a look. Perhaps I should briefly describe what these were like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, just the same translation issue as before. "Zurnali" should be translated as logbooks. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that "zurnali" should be translated as journal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the official CLSS position on that word.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have nothing against this kind of translation, and I ask the witness to explain what the journal or logbooks are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed. It's almost a case of what's in a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But let's proceed. They are what they are, whether you call them journals or logbooks. At the end of the day, we will have a look at them and know exactly in our mind what word to attribute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, I would like to ask you one thing. Can you just slow down a little while giving evidence. I'm sorry for interrupting you. This is precisely what I was about to tell you. Can you please pick up where you left off. I am not sure if you know where you left off, do you?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: When I got closer to that place, Brana had already finished his inspection of what he referred to as journals. So I proceeded to do the same thing. That is why I am certain what they look like, and I think if shown one now I could not possibly fail to identify this. This is large format sheet. They have a certain size, and in order to be stacked up like that they had to be folded three times, not just once. Each of the sheets had the month that it was in relation to and the order was chronological. Handwritten on every single sheet, the date that the sheet was in relation to starting, of course, with January on the top of the pile, and then spilling over into February and the order was consistently followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just another thing, I believe we have a small problem. Did you say that you could identify those journals, what they look like in terms of appearance? And can you please just repeat about their format, but please slow down if you can.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. These documents were not bound. They didn't have any covers. And they had a certain size and that's how they were stacked there, that's how they were stored there. They are one of a kind. The only document of that size being used, and in this they were different from all the other document that were circulating. They were in relation to each month separately. They were a reflection of the financial states of the hotel on daily basis and the order followed was chronological.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "daily financial situation," does this mean that a journal was drafted in relation to each day or a sheet, or each month had its own sheet? How did this work?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the hotel's business, it really depended whether a sheet could be filled on any particular day, and it was by no means certain that 30 sheets would equal a month. This was by no means a commitment. Each day had a sheet, but sometimes there were days when there were no guests or very few, so the entries made were not too numerous, and then they would go on like that. So a month has to comprise of every single day within that month, that was the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think you talked about whether these sheets were bound or whether they had covers. I may have missed that. But can you please tell me nevertheless, was there any system to the way these were stored and organised? Were they organised in a tidy way or not?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, there was a system to this, and it appeared to be a tidy system. There were some folders there, and so on and so forth; but as soon as I looked at it, I could realise that there was order there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you manage to track down all of the journals in relation to that year?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: One was missing, the July journal. I personally saw this for myself because I was sorting these month by month. I wasn't able to simply believe that July was missing, because everything else was there, but this was a very conspicuous absence and Brana before me had established the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. All right. That's what happened. You failed to track down the July journal. What did you do next? What steps did you take, if any?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: That same day, having left the management building, we agreed that we could obtain this information in a different form from the accountancy unit, from a different source, the accounts. Brana was not a qualified bookkeeper, so to speak. He was for the most part waitering. So he was not willing to infringe on anyone else's territory, special that of the accountants working there; but he knew them well so I pleaded with him to call them after I had left and to ask them over the following days to come there, to go to the cashiers unit, and to try to find any sort of information that they believe might be useful to us. He promised to do just that for me. Meanwhile, I had managed to get in touch with Risto Saremac, who at the time was at the Jahorina Olympic centre. He was the last manager of the hotel before the hotel went into administration. Mr. Saremac was quite kind with me, promising, yes, promising, that he would speak to his former employees, or, rather, the lady employees of the accountancy unit. He said that he was quite confident that they could do the job for us, that they could track the documents down for us because they were diligent worker and very systemic. He knew them well. He said Mijatovic, nothing for you to worry about, you will be getting this information in due course. The documentation was kept in order, everything was being done by the book, it was all tidy, the documents was tidy, and the archive was under lock and key. I took his word for it. And I held him to his promise, so I bade my time waiting for his invitation expecting that there would be end to this, and that the documents would be tracked down. I was convinced that this would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What happened next after you received some sort of information?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I learned in the meantime that the main account and the cashier helped Brana to locate and copy the documents and invoices at the accountancy department relating to the guests who stayed at the hotel in July of that year. Once they finished this, Brana called me by phone and that was about ten days after my departure. He told me that I could come over and take the copies of these accounting documents and that is precisely what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us how this handover of documents took place? Who gave you the copies of the documents?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived at the hotel, and Brana came out to meet me. I remember quite clearly, although some 20 months had elapsed since then. We were standing in the street, and he gave me these copies without any covering sheet. He told me this is it, this is what you were looking for; and I'm giving it to you. And it's finished. I took the documents from his hand and in front of him, just browsed through the documents superficially. I noticed these were invoices, the copies were not exactly good, and there were also some other documents containing names of persons. I suppose that those were supplements to the invoice or, rather, the documents on the basis of which these invoices were issued. There were reservation sheets or confirmations or whatever. Just like a delivery bill is part of an invoice, in hotel business these supplements always accompany invoices. I immediately saw that there was some 30-odd documents, I didn't count them. This is not -- neither a lot neither a few. I also noticed some bills relating to the use of restaurants and the bills relating to drinks and food.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you have a chance to look closely at these invoices? Can you describe these other documents that were attached to the invoices? Do you remember what they actually contained, who wrote them, who they were sent to?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: These other documents constituted less than a third of the documents. They were issued by the Bratunac Brigade. It was a typical format typed on each sheet saying that the following persons were given approval to spend the night at the hotel on specifying days according to the attached list. And these lists were different in terms of the number of persons and their names. This document was also certified by the brigade stamp and signed by the brigade officer in charge. I think that constituted a complete set of documents that served as a basis for providing services by the hotel and later on for charging for those services.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In order to avoid any confusion, in addition to these documents that you mentioned now issued by the Bratunac Brigade, was there any additional list attached thereto, or were these documents only what you saw, perhaps, you haven't been properly understood?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Those were A4 forms and nothing else other than that. And these were the copies that I took over. In no way could they be in any other format, either smaller or bigger, with different data and different shape, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, I shall be very brief. Given that you had an opportunity to see those journals earlier, can you tell me, among those copies, were any copies of the journals?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were no copies of the journal. I would have spotted them immediately because of the form. You have a sheet of paper folded three times. People might remember that payroll list used to be folded like that and they were printed. According to the French word, "journal."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpret's note that we didn't comprehend what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Stop, stop. You need to repeat a bit please because the interpreters had problems following you. I can tell you until where they -- where they caught up with you: "People might remember that payroll lists used to be folded like that and they were printed. According to the French word, 'journal.'" That is where it stops. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the definition of this term that we are interested in, that means journal, a diary, or an accountancy book that contains all daily financial changes according to a certain chronological order. And there is also the definition that it might mean a newspaper, a magazine, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, among the copies of the documents that you received, were any pages from the guest book?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that would have been possible. There were no journals and there were no pages taken out of the guest book because I would have recognized them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more question, please. Among these copies, were there any documents in which the name of Vujadin Popovic was mentioned, because that was basically the terms of reference of what you were instructed to look for and why you went there?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I did notice among the documents immediately that the name Vujadin Popovic appeared in a couple of places and that was sufficient for me in terms of the objective of our verification. And with that, I deemed my mission to be accomplished. I took them and handed them over further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In a nutshell, you said that you had been given some 30 documents, does that mean that the remaining documents did not contain the name of Vujadin Popovic?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, you and Mr. Brana Ilic, at the time when he handed over the copies to you, did the two of you compile any list or some document confirming that he had handed over the documents to you according to the specification; and, on the other hand, did you sign such a kind of document as the recipient of these documents?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: During the handover, we did not -- or, rather, Brana did not make any other additional documents that should have probably contained the specification of the documents attached to it. They were just copied without any attachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, tell us, did you handover these documents to someone else, and if you did to whom did you hand them over?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: When I first met you in Zvornik, I gave the documents to you in the same way as I received them from Brana without any written record of that. I just handed them over to you personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing, after that, were you given another assignment to go to the Fontana Hotel, and if you did, can you tell us when and why?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: After certain period of time or, rather, a long period of time, more precisely the following year, I was instructed to go to the same location and look again for the same documents and to make the same number of copies as I did the first time. I followed the same procedure as I did on the first occasion. I called Mr. Ilic first, and he called me back, very quickly, after a couple of days by telling me that the copies were made and waiting for me. And I had went there to collect them either on the same day or the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us were these the same documents that you had taken the previous year?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't expect anything different. I expected them to be identical in number and shape and the quality of copy without any attached documents that did not exist at the same -- during the first time, and I didn't expect them to appear the next time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "without any attachments," are you referring to the record of handover that would have been signed by you?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I was referring to, a record on the handover. It wasn't made on that occasion, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify things, you said that you had been instructed. Can you tell me who instructed you to go there?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic or, rather, you, told me that you had misplaced these documents. I accepted that, and I thought that this would be a very easy task and that is how I went and did it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, today in my office, I showed you a selection of documents that the OTP had obtained, and I read to you part of the statement given by Mr. Erin Gallagher, the OTP investigator who interviewed Mr. Brana Ilic about, inter alia, this handover of documents. I showed you these documents that Mr. Brana Ilic mentioned. Tell me, when you compared those documents and the documents that you received, can you tell me whether these are two identical sets of documents if -- and if there are any difference, what the differences are?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: These two sets of documents are identical. I could have seen that at the first glance and in every detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A couple of more questions relating to your testimony of the 6th of June and the 9th of June of this year. We have shown you a transcript of the part of your testimony in B/C/S, in the language that both of us speak, and you were able to read these two passages that were in dispute in a sort of way and reflected your testimony in a different manner from the one that you have given today. I am going to read to you this part of your testimony, and I would kindly ask you to tell me, because you indicated that there was some omissions, and therefore I would kindly ask you to explain to the Chamber what happened. That's the transcript of the 6th of June, 2008, page 21917, lines 2 to 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just confirm what this B/C/S transcript is? Is it the one that was transcribed by CLSS in their memo that we received today? Or is it the old one that we received this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is from -- it is, no, no. The transcript I was provided by OTP yesterday by Mr. McCloskey, but I believe that it is the same as the B/C/S version -- B/C/S version of translation unit. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the only difference is we provided a transcript of lines 2 to 10. CLSS only reviewed lines 5 to 10. So just to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 5 to 10. Yes, 5 to 10 is the subject of my question. It is just the answer, not the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you gave the following answer on that occasion: "The Fontana Hotel in Bratunac has been in the receivership since 2006, and it's still ongoing. Given this situation pertaining to this hotel, we managed with the assistance of its employees who are still on the list of employees of the hotel, to locate and take certified journals, the so-called journals of the guests staying overnight and the invoices relating to the guests who stayed at the hotel in June and July 1995." This is part of your testimony that was entered into the transcript on the 6th of June. You had an opportunity to see it, and can you tell me now how it happened that this version is completely different from the one that you have given us today? What is this all about?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Most probably this is due to imprecision, I would not like to call it lack of concentration. But apparently, during my long testimony I -- had I known that I should have been more precise at the time I should have and could have probably used some more precise words, and some words are actually missing. What does that mean? Obviously, there is some erroneous meaning attached to this, and it deviates from what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Just to clarify, Your Honour, the witness is suggesting that the words -- the words aren't missing from the transcript or from the audio, it was -- he didn't actually say them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you agree to that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't say the proper word at the time when he testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it's [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's clear enough. It's clear enough. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- error in transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, today I showed you the corrected -- or, rather, this version of the transcript, and I think you actually made copy of it and then you corrected it. Or, rather, you put in what you failed to say last time. Now, I don't know whether you can perhaps read this or maybe just say it or perhaps I should read out to you what you told me today and then you can confirm whether this is so or not. We sent this text to the Prosecution, so if they are not objecting.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the sentence went more or less like this. That in the business books, and then there is a list made, and the list includes the guest book, the journals, but there -- it should also say that instead of those documents that were supposed to exist there, the couple of documents that I mentioned, we found invoices. And then it goes on. So instead of the documents that we don't have, we have invoices. So I think that in this context we can now really say everything accurately so that everybody can understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just read the second sentence that should have been corrected, so let me just ask you whether this is what you said should have been said and wasn't said: "We are in such a statutory position of this hotel, and we managed to retrieve from the archives with the assistance of the workers who are still on the lists of the employees of the hotel, we managed to find and take the certified -- to take instead of certified journals, journals of the book of overnight stays, the invoices that pertain to the overnight stays of the guests in the period of June and July 1995."

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I think that's precisely how it is. So instead, and then I list the documents, we took the invoices.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me one more thing, the word "June" is mentioned in the transcript, and what you actually said is June, July [as interpreted]. So since this word "June" really was said, could you please explain to us what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I think since the previous time-period was mentioned, i.e., probably meant to say, but that is a different thing. That this was a period from the 1st until the 31st of July. But since I spoke about the time-period then the word "June" slipped in, and it was a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But could you please repeat once again, did you have any task to search through the documents pertaining to June 1995?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, never, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have just one more paragraph to give to the witness, but it is time for break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Provided you finish within the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, let me just show you the second paragraph from the transcript. That's at page 21946, the lines are 2 through 15. Again, we are only interested in one particular bit. Well, I will have to read the whole text: "The thing is of a technical nature, and the means to know what documents we need for what period and from what part of the archives, whether the cashiers desk, the accountancy, the auxiliary books or what. As we worked on collecting those documents, I ascertained that for July 1995, according to the statements made by employees of the hotel, somebody had - somebody they don't know who that is - had taken the journals, precisely the journals and the books pertaining to July, with the assistance of the police station in Bratunac a few years earlier. And those documents could not be found in the archives of the hotel. "However, the employees, the cashier, the account, and the others, managed to find copies of those documents from other sources -- or, rather, of invoices --" Instead of no, no that's not what it says in the original. I apologise: "Invoices, journals, the book of overnight stays of domestic guest, the book of overnight stays of foreign guests, and so on, and then we were able to put together everything that we needed, everything that we were supposed to get. So they were able to find it." Now, could you please tell me -- well, I've already read outside the word that I should not have read now, but I first had to ask you a question and then you were supposed to tell me. Could you please tell me whether this text, without this word that I read out, does that really reflect -- you mentioned that there is a difference between what you said then and what you say now. So could you please tell me what is it? Why -- what is it that in fact led to this confusion on your part?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I think that is the same thing as we had a little while ago. We were talking about the distinction between the documents that we didn't find and the documents that were available. As I listed them, I said we found invoices instead of -- I am not going to now list the documents that did not exist, that were not available. So I had to make that distinction whereas I did not do it at the time. So again it's the same thing as in the previous case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So does it mean that you did not say the word, "instead"?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did not make that distinction. I didn't use any words to mark that distinction, and I should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And just one more question for you, as I went through the transcript I noticed that you did not mention the letters that you described today, the approvals from the Bratunac Brigade that were attached to the bills or invoices. So could you please tell us why? Could you remember -- can you remember why this was not mentioned by you earlier?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I think that in the first testimony I did not mention the approvals issued by the Bratunac Brigade, the authorisations. They were an integral part of the documents that I received. I think I should have mentioned them, but it was precisely because of the precision that was lacking or that was suggested. I left them out. I don't know why, because they were in the minority in relation to other documents, the invoices.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mijatovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And so we will have the break now which needs to be of 30 minutes. It will be 30 minutes from now. Thank you. In other words, we can actually reconvene at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may proceed to cross-examine the witness if you so wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. McCloskey indicated that we may not have any questions, but we do have a few. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I have asked you. So please go ahead and take your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I'd just like to clarify with you first your testimony today. In 2000 -- in June 2008, you testified here that you had picked up or you obtained the guest logbooks for July 1995. That's what you testified in June, correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I received copies of the documents that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: You received copies of the guest logbooks for July 1995, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: No, did I not mention the guest logbooks. I did not say that I received them. I received invoices and the parts that have to do with the approvals or authorisations that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I just want to clarify, sir, in June 2008, you said you did receive copies of the guest logbooks and today you've told us that that was a mistake, and that you didn't receive those copies, correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise for having done that at that time. I did not do it on purpose. I did not intend to mislead anyone or to prejudice anyone in any way. The sense and the intention was to say things as they were, but it was not precise enough. And if I -- if anyone had asked me at that time to be more precise, I would have given the same answer as I did today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, I want to read out a question that was asked to you at transcript page 21945. Now, you've just said that if someone had asked you to be more precise, you would have given the same answer. Well, this was the question that you were asked: "Can you describe to me everything you know, everything you remember about those documents? You've obviously you've seen them. Precisely describe to me what they were, as far as you can recall?" Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And do you remember that that question drew an objection from Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall everything. I don't remember how it proceeded from there. I wish I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you made a mistake in your June 2008 testimony, and you made that mistake more than once, didn't you sir?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: It's one and the same thing. In one case when we were talking about the fact that instead of receiving the documents that we had sought that would have given us the date immediately, that we found and took the invoices. And in the other case, the sentence was the same, that we took the invoices instead of -- now, I don't want to list all the documents, the guest book, the journals, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And so when did you first communicate to Mr. Zivanovic that you had made this mistake?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not communicate that to Mr. Zivanovic. I thought -- well, I didn't have that in front of me, but to my mind it was sufficient, but then later on I don't know how the procedure was, but at any rate up to the day when they told me that I needed to provide some clarifications. And that was some time after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So today is the first time that you have spoken with the Defence about this issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment before you answer the question. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The witness answered differently. He indicated that there was a time when he communicated with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Exactly when did you discuss this issue with the Defence? Can you tell us how many times, over what period of time?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was several weeks later. I don't know the exact date. I don't know the exact date when I was told that I should provide some more precise answers to some of the questions. And since that time, we've had several contacts to discuss the procedure and how to explain that with greater precision because the first time we didn't do this in-depth. Not only in this case but in other cases, and we didn't get the broader context; and we did not go and get specific answers, what was done, who specifically was involved, by name and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: So what happened when you first spoke about this? Did Mr. Zivanovic tell you that there may have been an issue with the translation, or did he ask you for further clarification and you suggested that there was an issue or can you tell us how that conversation went?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
utterances.text: Well, translation was not brought up at all because I have nothing to do with it in terms of how my testimony was given, technically. But the thrust of the conversation was to clarify some definitions and some kinds. This was the most important part of documents that we were supposed to find and what we actually managed to find, what we couldn't find physically, and what was not accessible to us because after all what was important to us was to get results regardless of the actual source.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Sir, you told us today that in the documents that you received from Mr. Ilic, you saw references to Vujadin Popovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO MIJATOVIC
